thread.title: Wall Street Leans Forward Pre-Bell; Futures Green, Europe Higher, Asia Mixed

author: MT Newswires
title: Wall Street Leans Forward Pre-Bell; Futures Green, Europe Higher, Asia Mixed
text:
Shutterstock photo Wall Street pre-market Wednesday is leaning forward, with US stock market index futures pointing to an opening bell up perhaps 0.15% from Tuesday's close. European bourses are trading higher, while Asian exchanges closed mixed on the outlook for central bank policy in the US, Europe and Japan. The Federal Reserve is expected to announce a 0.25% rate-hike Wednesday at 2 pm ET. A federal judge gave a thumb's up to AT&T's ( T ) $85 billion buyout of Time Warner ( TWX ), which may provoke another round of industry mergers. Smartphone-maker ZTE resumed trading and fell 41.6% after its $1.4 billion settlement with the US government on trade violations. Bitcoin is trading for $6,465, oil is trading for $66.25 and 10-year US Treasuries offer 2.96%.
On the economic calendar are the MBA mortgage applications bulletin at 7 am ET, followed by the producer price index at 8:30 am, then the Atlanta Fed business inflation expectations report at 10 am. The much-watched EIA domestic oil inventories release is at 10:30 am.
Bitauto ( BITA ) and Korn/Ferry International ( KFY ) report earnings pre-bell, among
others.
In Europe, the British FTSE 100 is up 0.43%, the French CAC 40 is up 0.26% and the German DAX is up 0.20%.
In the futures, the S&P 500 is up 0.15%, the Nasdaq is up 0.27% and the Dow Jones Industrial Average is up 0.13%.
Asian stock markets were mixed Wednesday, ahead of Fed and European Central Bank policy decisions. The Bank of Japan is expected to leave policy unchanged. Hong Kong and Shanghai fell back, but Tokyo gained. Other exchanges were also mixed.
In Tokyo, the Nikkei 225 rose 0.38% on a softer yen, considered a positive in export-oriented Japan. The US Federal Reserve's expected rate-hike may further soften the yen, said analysts.
The benchmark Nikkei 225 rose 88.03 to 22,966.38, as gaining issues outnumbered losers 146 to 68.
Leading the upside were deliver-service Nippon Express (NPEXY, 9062:Tokyo), up 7.0%, followed by tech-and-finance shop Softbank (SFTBY, 9584:Tokyo), up 2.8%, and then plumbing-fixtures house Toto (TOTDF, 5332:Tokyo), up 2.6%.
On the downside were chemical concern Denka (4061:Tokyo), off 3.2%, and then silicon-wafer maker Sumco (SUMCF, 3436:Tokyo), off 3.1%.
In market news, Toshiba (TOSYY, 6502:Tokyo), disclosed a $6.3 billion stock buyback, financed by proceeds from an $18 billion sale of its memory-chip business, and finished up 6.7%.
The Hong Kong Hang Seng Index fell back 1.22% on prospects for a stronger Hong Kong dollar, and as smartphone-maker ZTE tumbled 41.6% on heavy trading volume after the company agreed to pay $1.4 billion in fines to the US government for violating trade sanctions against North Korea and Iran.
The Hong Kong dollar is pegged to the US greenback, so tightening by the Federal Reserve will also result in higher interest rates in Hong Kong, affecting the business scene of the former crown colony, said analysts.
The broad gauge Hang Seng fell 377.91 to 30,721.15, as losing issues outnumbered gainers 47 to two.
On the upside were old-line conglomerate Swire Pacific (19:HK), up 0.5%, and then utility-conglomerate Power Assets Holdings (6:HK), up 0.3%.
On the downside were Apple ( AAPL )-supplier AAC Technologies (2018:HK), off 4.1%, followed by PetroChina (85:HK), off 3.0%, and then CSPC Pharmaceutical (1093:HK), off 2.7%,
On the mainland, the Shanghai Composite fell 0.97% to 3,049.80.
China's GDP is expected to expand by 6.6% in 2018, reported the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, citing a survey of economists.
On the other exchanges, the S. Korean Kospi was closed; the Taiwan TWSE rose 0.26%; the Australian ASX 200 declined 0.51%; the Singapore Straits Times Index fell 1.11%; and the Thai Set declined 0.52%. In late trading in Mumbai, the Sensex was up 0.17%.
